Dynamic world physics closeout: Make supported worlds move and react.
Author physical objects, constraints, projectiles, destruction, lightning, grass, fire, fog and liquids; Play and exported games share runtime behavior.
See PHYSICS-CLOSEOUT-CHECKS-20260927.md for 772 core checks and the visible/editor/export evidence. Test counts are not universal certification.
Bounded closeout passes; mesh/textures next, performance last. Fixed fluid domains, conservative collision and unsupported-fracture fallback remain.
Character movement and grappling: Move continuously through an authored world.

WASD and live facing drive movement; Shift sprints, Space jumps, V dodges or lunges, Control changes posture or slides, and G grapples. Resources and traversal states are shared between Play and the standalone player.
Controller, collision, terrain, moving anchors, camera and runtime presentation are connected; source and dated checks are separate evidence.
Step 4 accepted within documented scope; current physics closeout fixtures pass
Telegraph combat and combat actors: Fight and heal while moving using visible aimed areas.

Player attack uses a repeating 2.5-second cycle; release completes the current cycle. Enemy Swipe uses 1.5 seconds. Cones follow live caster position/facing and fill with channel progress. Friendly damage/healing are blue/green; hostile damage/healing red/orange.
Runtime health, target selection, pursuit, collision, line of sight, breakable objects and healing share the adventure runtime without changing saved scene definitions.
Step 4A accepted with agreed placeholder damage/health; current exported combat checks pass
Crowd control and boss break bars: Apply explicit control restrictions and coordinated boss vulnerability windows.

Stun, knockback, pull, launch, knockdown, root, slow, silence, fear, taunt, sleep, blind, disorient and tether have separate rules. Player immunity follows control; boss CC instead damages an intact 1,000-point bar, with up to eight seconds stagger, 25 percent extra damage and 90-second refill.
CombatControl, CombatActor and BossBreakBar connect runtime actions and displays. Friendly/self CC protection, player anti-chain rules and boss contribution rules are separate.
Implemented runtime components and integrations; exact current test outcomes and remaining acceptance are reported separately
Discoverable editor help: Find a way forward without leaving the project.
Help / Tutorials and F1 open optional searchable lessons, with Back, Next, Restart and saved reading positions. Close or Escape returns to creating.
Shared controls remain available across current editing experiences. Stable lesson IDs preserve progress through catalog changes; malformed preferences fall back safely.
Implemented text guidance; live UI acceptance pending. Not animated demonstrations, guided task detection or the full three-mode startup
Walk and build preview: Make building part of exploring the world.
Walk at player height, right-drag to look, and use existing editing tools. Play starts a separate test; Pause restores authored objects at the tested viewpoint.
Shares scene data, Undo, asset insertion and snapping. Returning to ordinary editing preserves authored changes. Core checks cover viewpoint/data separation, not full GUI acceptance.
Experimental code foundation; live input and visual review, objectives, experience and unlocks remain pending
Adventure gameplay foundation: Make a small playable adventure without writing code.

New starter adventure creates a key, door and exit level with save protection. Existing scenes can opt into walking controls; Beginner and Advanced expose different settings on the same data. Play uses WASD, right-drag and E.

Static-box collision and key links use an independent play copy; Reset preserves authored objects. The starter path has code-driven walking and interaction checks, distinct from human usability review.
Bounded authored rules plus the movement and combat foundation described below; not arbitrary scripting or the complete Interactive building experience
Windows adventure export: Share an authored adventure as a standalone Windows game.
Export playable game writes a new folder with a player, engine/runtime libraries and portable scene content. Existing folders are refused; missing runtime files abort the export.

The player shares movement and interaction code with the editor. Package hashes and content validation are diagnostic integrity checks, not signatures. Hidden startup rendering is distinct from visible input verification.
Windows x64 / Direct3D 12 foundation; clean-machine, signing, other platforms and visible player acceptance remain unverified
Reusable assets and scene composition: Reuse authored content across scenes without rebuilding it.

Browse a remembered folder with text/type filters. Insert models, native templates/groups or scene objects; copy/paste selections during an editor session; repair missing models; export portable scene/selection folders.

Insertions receive independent identities and one Undo. Groups retain spacing and translated routes. Portable folders carry embedded GLBs and hash manifests; editor-session copied models retain original file references.
Implemented bounded content workflow; thumbnails and imported-model templates remain outside scope; Windows adventure packaging is tracked separately
Native application and build: The desktop application used to create and preview scenes.
Open the native editor through its launcher. The active product is native C++; Python is build/analysis tooling.
The editor uses the scene core and NativeSession; the separate project host loads native project modules.
Classic creator interface: Keep world creation approachable and familiar.

Use floating Builder, Characters, Environment and More menus over the canvas. Simple settings hide advanced transforms/body controls. Terrain and Shapes have dedicated gear panels; named colors and quality choices replace numeric labels.
Controls edit authored scene data. Advanced disclosure preserves hidden properties; the feature catalogue also contains future ideas.
Implemented workflow; broader polish remains bounded by tested cases
Independent game preview: Preview the authored scene inside the editor.
Play uses the existing editor canvas and session in both windowed and fullscreen modes. Pause holds simulation; Reset returns to the authored start.
Retained GamePreview support is not the active Play command path. Inline preview is not a packaged executable export.
Implemented inline workflow; exhaustive parity remains open
Scene data and compatibility: Represent the world the user has authored.
A scene contains objects, terrain, pours, environment and rendering preferences. Character records also represent shapes/effects; a record is not necessarily an animated person.
Scene JSON is separate from renderer packets and project manifests. Authored state is separate from transient simulation.
Scene packet ABI: Carry prepared scene geometry and settings into the native viewport.
The editor writes the V7 binary scene packet; the parser retains V1–V7 support. The scene JSON schema and project schema use independent version numbers.
The packet connects editor geometry to GPU resource creation and viewport rendering.
Local automation: Allow local tools or an assistant to inspect and edit scenes consistently.
Describe capabilities, inspect a scene, or apply a validated command batch: add, move, route, rename, remove, configure, shape, transform, terrain brush, water and stamp.
Commands use expected scene hashes and persistence rules; they do not embed an AI provider or duplicate every GUI action.
Partial product coverage: implemented local commands
Persistence and editing safety: Save work and reverse or cancel edits.
Use save/open and undo/redo. Brushes are transactions; canceled work can return to the previous scene. Save/Discard/Cancel protects replacement/closing; stale scene writes are rejected.
Scene history stores scene state; validation and atomic file replacement protect persistence. It is not a bounded delta-history system.
Implemented workflows; long-session memory remains a concern
Terrain authoring: Build and paint the ground of a scene.
Raise/lower, smooth, flatten and paint terrain; place hill/crater/plateau stamps or stamp a selected shape. Terrain brush settings are independent from object sculpt settings.
The 97×97 authored heightfield becomes a 193×193 display mesh. Physics uses collision tiles; liquid surfaces use the terrain as their bed.
Partial terrain system: finite heightfield, no streamed world/caves
Object geometry and sculpting: Place solids precisely and reshape their actual mesh.

Translate, rotate, scale and snap objects. Pull, Push, Smooth and Flatten edit a mesh copy; undo/cancel preserves the source asset. Starter placement is bounded and supports adjustable grid spacing. Rotation handles can snap their edited axis on release; grouped placement preserves relative spacing.
Transforms affect rendering, bounds and collision preparation. Sculpting is separate from terrain height brushes.
Partial sculpting system: core brushes and placement
Props and effects: Populate scenes with basic geometry, nature and visual effects.
Place basic solids, rock/boulder/pebble/grass objects, fire/light/lava helpers, Chaos Lightning, Chaos Rock, Light-Bound Shard and Craxis Smoke.

Procedural geometry, materials, lights and volumes create these appearances. Supported fracture and wind/contact grass motion now have explicit physics checks; asset appearance upgrades remain Task 2.
Implemented prop set; broader nature systems planned
Static model import: Bring a model into the scene as preview geometry.
Choose a GLB model, validate it, then place and transform instances. The importer handles static mesh geometry and validates its buffers/accessors/hierarchy.
Imported objects feed scene geometry and optional sculpt/collision preparation. Creator import is distinct from skinned character runtimes.
Partial asset pipeline: static GLB preview
Render ownership and updates: Keep rendering and simulation working while the UI processes interaction.
A session receives coalesced scene/camera/playback changes, renders frames and exposes status/capture. Hidden preview sessions can suspend and resume.
The session coordinates physics, flow and viewport submission. Scene refresh and resize still contain expensive reconstruction paths.
Implemented ownership; optimization and failure recovery incomplete
Native rendering contract: Render actual frames at the chosen display resolution.
Current acceptance requires render/output dimensions to match, no super resolution and no frame generation. HDR scene shading and spatial edge smoothing precede presentation.
Native-resolution RR is an optional denoiser, not permission to enable spatial upscaling. Existing runtime vendor source is not proof it is active in the editor.
Implemented configuration; dated visible benchmark evidence is workload-specific
Inline hardware ray tracing: Offer a selectable quality ladder for ray-based lighting.

Choose Off, Low, Medium, High or Path tracing. The implementation ranges from direct visibility to AO/reflections, diffuse GI and sampled multi-bounce opaque transport; freeze/bounce settings support reference views.
Inline compute RayQuery uses BLAS/TLAS geometry, then passes noisy lighting and guides to denoising. Unsupported capability can fall back to raster.
Partial rendering system: implemented tiers, bounded materials
Native temporal denoiser: Stabilize noisy ray-traced lighting without vendor reconstruction.
Mode 0 selects the native temporal wavelet path: prefilter, history reprojection/rejection, atrous filtering and composition.
Depth, normal, motion and material guides support temporal decisions. Emission/history handling is part of the rendering pipeline.
Implemented algorithm; dated native-wavelet diagnostic runs passed, broader quality and stability remain unverified
Optional native Ray Reconstruction: Offer an alternative vendor denoiser at native resolution.
Mode 1 requests NVIDIA RR through NGX at 1:1 input/output dimensions. Missing or failed support can fall back to the native filter with status reporting.
RR depends on local SDK/runtime availability and guide buffers. Preserve ABI 0=wavelet, 1=RR.
Implemented optional integration; portability and current runtime validation bounded
Atmosphere and lighting: Set scene mood and illuminate the world.
Configure time of day/day cycle, fog, local lights and smoke. Water/lava/chaos appearances combine procedural shading, emission and explicit lighting.
Atmosphere injection/integration/composition follows the surface rendering path. Raster proxy shadows differ from triangle visibility in RT.
Partial atmosphere: bounded froxels/lights, no full weather/smoke simulation
Rigid-body simulation: Let configured props fall, tumble and interact with collision geometry.
Body settings and density feed Jolt fixed-step simulation. Terrain/prop collision preparation runs asynchronously; playback/reset separates simulation from authored placement.
Body poses update scene transforms and liquid obstacle/coupling inputs. Collision geometry can approximate visual meshes.
Bounded physics and lifecycle closeout fixtures pass; arbitrary-scale performance remains unverified
Water and lava flow: Pour finite water/lava and observe terrain-bound movement.
Arm a pour, click the ground, then Play/Pause/Reset. Separate water/lava fields evolve on a 48×48 grid, with obstacle coverage and liquid geometry.
Terrain elevation and sampled solid occupancy guide transport; the physics wrapper uses liquid data for approximate body coupling.
Partial simulation: surface flow, not general 3D fluids
Routes and simulation controls: Make placed objects traverse authored paths during preview.
Draw X/Z routes, set speed, Play/Pause/Reset, optionally repeat or follow a character. Escape cancels active operations before leaving fullscreen.
Routes drive transforms separately from skeletal animation and navmesh/character collision. Route completion and fluids have distinct playback concerns.
Partial movement system: authored routes and controls
Local music: The dedicated player provides track selection, playlist next, play/pause, stop and volume.
Windows MCI supplies local playback; this is editor media, not a spatial sound or exported soundtrack engine.
Texture foundation: Load compressed texture data correctly in supported rendering paths.
DDS BC5/BC7 handling preserves authored mips and uses format-aware uploads/views; image-loading fallback remains.
The separate runtime texture path is broader than editor procedural materials. A loader does not supply a full terrain PBR library or streaming manager.
Project host boundary: Launch native projects with selected scenes and presets.
Choose a project manifest, choose a scene, reconcile/check/save preset settings and launch the native host. Empty is the project module in this tree; other project folders are built when present.
Project schema 3 and .startest settings belong to the project workflow. A creator .starscene is not automatically exported into a standalone game.
Persistent CPU workers: Reuse CPU threads for parallel preparation.
Persistent range workers divide contiguous work, let the caller participate and join at completion. Actual participation depends on requested workers and grain sizes.
Jolt and asynchronous collision cooking have separate concurrency budgets. This is not a universal task graph or work-stealing scheduler.
Implemented pool; general scheduling roadmap pending
Command recording and GPU lifetime: Submit GPU work while preserving resource ownership.
Frame slots, command allocators/lists, barriers and fences order GPU work. CPU preparation may be parallel while recording/submission remains serial.
Future parallel recording needs reserved bindings and per-worker/per-slot ownership, not simply more CPU threads.
Diagnostics and existing audits: Explain failures and retain reproducible evidence.
Native suites test core data, diagnostics, textures, sessions and classic UI; the audit harness records isolated runs, process measurements and renderer comparisons.
Saved tests identify exactly what was reached/passed/failed. This knowledge tool reads them; it does not rerun them.
Diagnostic benchmark path: Attempt unattended measurement without background presentation throttling.
The diagnostic path exposes benchmark controls and auditOffscreen; historical failures and subsequent visible-run results must be distinguished by date and workload.

The 22 September reliability checkpoint documents debug-confirmed invalid backbuffer use and an isolated output-target correction; that historical finding does not establish the outcome of later lifecycle checks. Consult the dated runtime evidence for current bounded results.
Implemented diagnostic path; broader reliability validation incomplete
